stem.text: An antibiotic enters bacterial cells through a membrane channel protein, P.
Some bacterial cells have shown resistance to this antibiotic by acquiring a mutation which alters P. This mutation prevents the entry of the antibiotic into the cell.
Which conclusions can be drawn about how resistance to this antibiotic developed in these bacteria?

items: The mutation changed the order of the amino acids in the gene coding for P.
The mutation resulted in the production of P with an altered tertiary structure.
The antibiotic is a hydrophobic molecule and so cannot cross the phospholipid bilayer to enter the cell.
